skill.name: companies-hiring-sdrs
skill.description: Find companies with recent sales or business development representative openings and confirm posting dates on their careers pages. Identify sales leaders and see the email status reported by Leadsets. Requires a paid Leadsets plan with scrape units.
skill.summary: Confirm recent SDR and BDR openings and identify sales leaders at the companies hiring.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: All 27 static alerts are false positives for the cited risks. The skill documents Leadsets network access, but the flagged lines show no shell execution, environment reads, or host reconnaissance. A separate privacy concern remains: contact exports lack explicit checks for destination and sharing permissions.

remediation.issue: The CSV default and optional Google Sheets output do not define how to approve the contact export destination or its visibility.
remediation.suggestion: Keep results in chat by default. Ask before exporting named contact data and confirm the file path or sheet and who can access it. Let users omit email addresses.

semantic_findings.title: Contact exports lack destination and sharing checks
semantic_findings.description: The skill lists CSV as a default despite later saying to export only on request. A Google Sheet could expose named contacts to unintended viewers if its sharing settings are not checked.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The export directions specify names and email addresses but do not require checking the destination or who can access it. No evidence of actual disclosure was found.

content.user_title: Find Companies Hiring SDRs and BDRs
content.value_statement: Company search results alone do not show whether a recent sales role is still open. Check careers pages for dated SDR and BDR openings, then find relevant sales leaders with Leadsets.
actual_capabilities: Searches for candidate companies by industry, headcount, location, and technology, or starts from a supplied list of domains.
Confirms open SDR and BDR roles from careers pages and records each matching title and posting date.
Finds up to three sales leaders per confirmed company by default and reports why each person matched.
Shows the email status and check date returned by Leadsets and can filter for addresses already marked verified.
Reports how many candidates were checked, how many companies qualified, and what search records and scrape units were used.
limitations: Confirming jobs requires a paid Leadsets plan with scrape units.
An unreadable careers page or a missing posting date prevents confirmation.
The skill does not enrich or independently verify emails.
The skill does not write or send outreach or push contacts to a CRM or sequencer.

use_cases.title: Prioritize sales accounts
use_cases.description: Find companies in your target market that posted SDR roles recently. Review the postings and relevant sales leaders before deciding which accounts to contact.

use_cases.title: Review a client account list
use_cases.description: Check a set of client-supplied domains for recent BDR openings. Report unreadable careers pages separately from confirmed results.

use_cases.title: Track hiring in a market segment
use_cases.description: Compare recent posting dates across qualifying companies. Use the match reasons and email statuses to review contact records before any export.

prompt_templates.title: Find recent SDR openings
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with the default market and lookback period.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find US B2B companies with 20 to 200 employees that posted SDR or BDR roles in the last 30 days. Show the role and posting date in chat only.

prompt_templates.title: Check a list of domains
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate existing accounts without searching for new companies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check these domains for open BDR roles posted in the last 14 days: [domains]. Report unreadable careers pages separately. Return results in chat only.

prompt_templates.title: Find leaders in a specific industry
prompt_templates.scenario: Narrow the market and review contacts by seniority.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find US fintech companies with 50 to 250 employees that posted SDR roles in the last 21 days. Return up to two revenue leaders per company with titles and match reasons. Show email status without addresses. Keep results in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Run a search with a usage cap
prompt_templates.scenario: Control research costs and review results before exporting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Leadsets usage and review at most 15 candidate domains for SDR or BDR openings posted in the past 30 days. Return revenue leaders with addresses already marked verified. Show confirmed companies without a matching leader separately. Report search records and scrape units used. Ask before creating or sharing a spreadsheet.

output_examples.input: Check these 12 domains for BDR openings from the last 14 days. Show posting dates and sales leaders without email addresses.
output: Example result: 12 domains checked, 3 companies confirmed, and 2 careers pages unreadable.
Northstar Metrics: BDR posted May 14. Priya Shah, Head of Sales, matched the requested function and seniority.

output_examples.input: Find SDR openings posted in the last seven days across these 10 domains.
output: Example result: No qualifying openings confirmed across 10 domains.
Nine careers pages were readable, but none showed a matching open role with a posting date in the window.
One careers page could not be read. Consider widening the search to 30 days.

best_practices: Specify your market, company size, and lookback period before starting.
Review posting dates and contact match reasons before using the results.
Check export permissions and omit email addresses when they are not needed.
anti_patterns: Treating a company search match as proof of a current opening.
Treating catch-all or unknown addresses as verified.
Exporting named contacts to a shared sheet without checking who can access it.

faq.question: What do SDR and BDR mean?
faq.answer: SDR means sales development representative. BDR means business development representative.

faq.question: What Leadsets access do I need?
faq.answer: Connect the Leadsets MCP server or use a Leadsets API key. Job confirmation requires a paid plan with scrape units.

faq.question: What happens when I give only company domains?
faq.answer: The skill skips company search, checks usage, and reviews the supplied companies for qualifying openings.

faq.question: What makes an opening confirmed?
faq.answer: The careers page must show an open role with a matching title and a posting date inside the requested window.

faq.question: Does the skill verify email addresses?
faq.answer: No. It reports the status Leadsets returns and can filter for addresses already marked verified.

faq.question: Can I request a CSV or Google Sheet?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify the output format and destination. For a shared sheet, confirm who should have access before exporting contact details.
